recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR-core source change is needed unless a future work group decision changes the restricted FHIRPath discriminator model; duplicate local prose would risk drift from the authoritative ElementDefinition, Profiling, and FHIRPath sections.
issue_request: FHIR-3526 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification FHIR-core StructureDefinition issue asking that slice discriminator syntax stop implicitly jumping through ResourceReference to the referenced resource, so profiles could discriminate on elements or extensions carried on the reference itself. The approved DSTU-era direction was to make reference traversal explicit while allowing extension-based discriminator paths on the reference element.
initial_application: The Jira comments say the issue was already applied in October 2014. No commit explicitly names FHIR-3526, but commit 365400a19a in the same historical window updated discriminator examples to distinguish reference-target paths such as item.reference.name from reference-entry extension paths such as item.extension.url.
additional_context: Current FHIR has replaced the old ResourceReference wording with Reference and represents discriminator paths as a restricted FHIRPath subset. Later related work, including FHIR-23035 and FHIR-27532, clarified resolve() behavior and simple FHIRPath consistency without reversing the explicit-reference-traversal model.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit. The current ElementDefinition source defines discriminator.path as a simple-subset FHIRPath expression; profiling.html allows extension(url) for extensions and resolve() for crossing resource boundaries, with examples separating item.extension(...) from item.resolve().code; and fhirpath.html lists both .extension("url") and .resolve() as allowed functions in the restricted subset.

related_jiras.note: Clarified how resolve() in discriminator paths refers to targetProfile-constrained referenced resources, reinforcing explicit reference traversal.
Aligned simple FHIRPath and ElementDefinition discriminator path documentation, reinforcing that discriminator paths use the restricted FHIRPath subset.
